draft.title: The Australian Human Rights Commission
card: The Australian Human Rights Commission is an independent statutory body of the Commonwealth. It was set up by federal law to work on human rights and discrimination.
Complaints

It investigates complaints of unlawful discrimination under federal laws. It first tries to settle a complaint by conciliation, which is a private process where both sides talk with help from a neutral person.
Education
It teaches the public, schools and workplaces about human rights, so that people know their rights and duties.
Reporting
It reports on human rights issues and gives advice to the government. The Commission is not a court, so it cannot make a binding ruling on a complaint.
draft.remember: The Commission handles complaints, educates and reports, but it does not decide cases like a court.

a.q: Which of these is a function of the Australian Human Rights Commission?
opts: Investigating complaints of unlawful discrimination
Hearing appeals against decisions of the High Court
Passing new laws to protect human rights
Punishing people found guilty of discrimination
a.why: The Commission investigates complaints of unlawful discrimination and tries to settle them. It does not pass laws, which is the work of parliament, and it is not a court, so it cannot punish people or hear appeals.
a.clue: The Commission is not a court and not a parliament.

b.q: Priya complains to the Commission that her employer treated her unfairly because of her race. Her employer refuses to settle after conciliation. What can the Commission itself do?
opts: Not make a binding ruling, as it is not a court
Order the employer to pay Priya compensation
Fine the employer for breaking the law
Change the law so that the employer must settle
b.why: The Commission investigates and tries to settle complaints, but it is not a court and cannot make a binding ruling. Ordering compensation or fining is tempting, but those are powers of a court, not of the Commission.
b.clue: Think about what kind of body the Commission is.

b.best: Not make a binding ruling, as it is not a court

problems.detail: The question asks what the Commission 'can' do, but the intended answer is something it cannot do ('Not make a binding ruling'). This is confusing and grammatically awkward. A clearer stem would be 'Which of these is true about the Commission?' or 'What can the Commission not do?'
The right option is the only one that gives a reason ('as it is not a court'), and it echoes the card and the clue almost word for word. A student could pick it without understanding the idea.

The why says fining is a power of a court here. In federal discrimination cases the Federal Court can award compensation, but unlawful discrimination is civil, not criminal, so employers are not fined. Grouping fines with compensation could mislead students.
